title: Why the Monsoon Comes

endcard.line: Footage: Mathanprasath K (CC BY 4.0); NOAA/CIRA (public domain)

segments.say: Every June, the wind over India turns around. And a whole country waits for it.
Through spring, the land heats up much faster than the sea. Hot air over the land rises, and the pressure there falls.
So cooler, wet air from the ocean is pulled in towards the land. That inflow is the south-west monsoon.
It usually reaches Kerala around the first of June, and covers the whole country by about the eighth of July.
When these winds meet the Western Ghats, they rise, cool, and pour rain on the sea-facing side. The far side stays much drier. That is a rain shadow.
From June to September, India gets about three-quarters of its rain for the whole year.
For your answer: the land heats, pressure falls, sea winds rush in, and the hills wring out the rain.

sources: IMD: normal onset over Kerala 1 June; covers the country by 8 July (normal dates revised 2020)
IMD: June–September brings about 75% of India's annual rainfall
NCERT Class 11, Fundamentals of Physical Geography / India Physical Environment, chapter on climate

quiz.q: What starts the south-west monsoon's inflow?
options: The sea heats faster than the land
The land heats faster than the sea, lowering pressure over it
quiz.why: Hot air over the land rises, pressure falls, and cooler wet sea air is pulled in.

quiz.q: When does the monsoon normally reach Kerala?
quiz.why: IMD's normal onset over Kerala is 1 June; it covers the country by about 8 July.

quiz.q: About how much of India's yearly rain falls from June to September?
quiz.why: June to September brings about 75% of the year's rain.

reviewNote: Facts were read against IMD's normal onset and rainfall pages and the NCERT climate chapter. Diagrams are schematic, with no map. Moving facts: IMD's normal onset dates were revised in 2020 and may be revised again.
